answer: Leaf-Anchored Neighbor Quotient: each identity's reach is capped by the distinct-neighborhood diversity of its declared peers, scored as a nebula of short-hop paths. An agent accepts work only from nodes whose local clustering maps cleanly onto a willow-like branching pattern with no repeated parent edges. Sybils that clone an honest peer cluster collapse their own quotient, since copied edges yield zero novel neighbors. The attacker must recruit genuinely independent operators at roughly one real neighbor per identity to stay visible, a walnut of cost that scales linearly with fleet size.
